subject: Supplier portal activation: possible homoglyph domain caused duplicate account
messages:
From: Rita Gomez <rita@pennylane-supply.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Accounts Payable <accounts-payable@pennylane-supply.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Problem accepting Coupa invite (email alias?)

Hi Vivek,

We accepted the supplier portal invite you sent earlier today but when we log in we see a blank supplier record and our PO field is not visible. The invite email came to rita@pennylane-supply.com, but when I ran a quick check I noticed our corporate domain is actually pennyläne-supply.com (we recently migrated and the umlaut remained in our marketing domain). I suspect the invite got routed to the ASCII equivalent and a new account was created with the wrong domain.

I attached a quick screenshot of the portal after login (screenshot-invite-accepted.png). We also exported the account list from our side (account-list-extract.csv) that shows two entries: one with rita@pennylane-supply.com and another with rita@xn--pennylne-supply-9k0b.com (the punycode form).

Can you check whether the invite landed on the correct tenant or if our account was split? We have an urgent PO (#PL-7783) that needs visibility.

Thanks,
Rita Gomez
Head of Finance | PennyLane Supply
rita@pennylane-supply.com
+1 415-555-0136

Forwarding Rita's note. Quick summary: PennyLane has a domain with an umlaut and their invite appears to have been normalized, creating two supplier identities (ascii + punycode). PO PL-7783 is blocked.

Ben / Laura — can you triage? If this is a tenant/account split we should: 1) confirm which supplier id is attached to the invite we sent, 2) merge or map the punycode/normalized identity to their canonical account, and 3) re-run the activation so PO fields surface. If we need Coupa support, escalate and request account merge on their side (they can handle punycode mapping).

I included the vendor attachments they sent.

Thanks — Vivek

Subject: Re: Problem accepting Coupa invite (email alias?)

Hi Rita — thanks for the details and the attachments, that was helpful.

Quick update on our side: I pulled the supplier index for PennyLane and I do see two supplier records that look like what you described. One was created with the normalized ascii domain (pennylane-supply.com) and one with the punycode form (xn--pennylne-supply-9k0b.com). It appears the invite token you received was associated with the ascii record.

Action plan:
- I'll open a ticket with Coupa support requesting a supplier merge and crosswalk of email addresses so the two records become a single supplier id. I'll pass through the supplier ids and the invite token you received.
- In parallel, Laura will create a temporary manual PO visibility grant on the ascii record so your AP team can see PL-7783 while Coupa performs the merge.
- After the merge we will re-issue a new invite from the canonical supplier id and confirm with you.

Couple of asks for you: can you confirm which email address your team uses for AP and whether you want the canonical address to be the umlaut (pennyläne-supply.com) or the ascii equivalent? Also, if you can share the invite message headers (we only need the Received/Message-ID) that will speed up Coupa's mapping.

I'll create the Coupa ticket now and paste the reference below.

—Ben

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Problem accepting Coupa invite (email alias?) — Ticket COU-91427

Hi Ben — ticket COU-91427 created. Thanks for the diagnostic notes and the account export.

Summary of findings: Coupa treats the punycode form of internationalized domains as distinct identifiers by default. We see two supplier ids: S-44092 (ascii) and S-44107 (punycode). The invite token supplied by Redwood maps to S-44092. We can perform a supplier merge and map the additional email addresses to the canonical supplier id but we need written authorization from PennyLane to perform the account-level merge.

Next steps we need from you (vendor authorization) and we'll proceed:
1) PennyLane to confirm via reply to this thread with which email to keep as canonical and an authorized signatory (name/title).
2) Once we have written consent we will perform the merge and propagate historical POs/attachments to the canonical id.
3) We'll then invalidate existing tokens and notify Redwood so you can issue a fresh invite.

Temporary workaround (what Laura can do): Coupa support confirmed we can give the ascii record (S-44092) a temporary PO visibility grant for PL-7783 for 48 hours while the vendor signs off.

Happy to coordinate the merge during business hours.

Regards,
Miguel Santos
Platform Support Engineer | Coupa Support
